Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

CaseBasedReasoning (development version)

New features

  • predict_outcome() predicts class and numeric outcomes from the k most similar training cases: a (tricube-weighted) majority vote with class probabilities, or a (weighted) mean. evaluate() scores the predictions on test data (accuracy, Brier score and log loss; RMSE and MAE) and delegates to evaluate_survival() for survival endpoints. predict() gains type = c("cases", "outcome", "survival"); the default still returns the similar cases (#43).
  • GowerModel and gower_distance(): the model-free Gower (1971) distance for mixed data (numeric, nominal, ordinal and logical variables, optional weights) as a baseline for the model-derived distances. Ranges come from the training cases, so query distances do not depend on the batch. All CBR methods (retrieval, outcome and survival prediction, counterfactuals, explain_match()) work with it (#44).

Bug fixes

  • Ordered factors in queries stay ordered. Queries were converted to unordered factors when aligned to the training data, which changed the design matrix of regression models fitted with ordered factors.

CaseBasedReasoning 0.5.0

Bug fixes

  • Factor values in queries are now matched to the training data by level name instead of internal integer code. Queries with different or dropped factor levels previously got silently wrong distances. Unknown levels are now an error (#4).
  • Character predictors no longer break distance calculation after fit() (#5).
  • Training cases with missing values are excluded consistently from fitting, distance calculation and retrieval. A single NA used to make get_similar_cases() fail. Missing values in the query are now an informative error (#6).
  • get_similar_cases() validates k: it must be a whole number and at most the number of training cases (#7).
  • get_similar_cases(merge = TRUE) works for queries without endpoint columns (#8).
  • variable_selection() now returns the variables retained by rms::fastbw() instead of all variables. Further arguments are passed on to fastbw(), and update = TRUE restricts the model to the selected variables (#9).
  • proximity_distance() converts proximity to distance as sqrt(1 - p). It previously used sqrt(max(p) - p), so distances depended on the observations in the batch. Absolute distance values change; the neighbour order within a query does not (#10).
  • Depth distance no longer loses the edge counts of earlier trees in forests with more than one tree. Depth distances were too small, and neighbour rankings could be wrong (#28).
  • weighted_distance() defaults to equal weights instead of 1, 2, ..., p and checks the length of weights (#14).
  • RFModel no longer forces verbose = TRUE for ranger (#15).
  • The threads argument of distance_random_forest() only applies to that call, and the previous RcppParallel setting is restored (#17).
  • Regression weights for numeric variables are no longer double-named (#18).
  • Depth distance no longer precomputes a table over all pairs of terminal nodes. Edge counts are computed on demand from each tree’s parent and depth arrays: n = 1500 with 100 trees now takes seconds instead of not finishing, and memory is linear in the number of nodes (#12).
  • orderMatrix() honours sortDirection in TBB builds and clamps k to the number of rows (#25).
  • Corrected the DOI of Englund & Verikas (2012) (#19).

New features

  • get_counterfactual_cases() returns the nearest training cases whose outcome differs from the query’s: a different class, a numeric outcome differing by at least min_diff, or a different event status at horizon for survival endpoints (Keane & Smyth, 2020). If the query has no outcome, it is predicted from its most similar cases (#23).
  • explain_match(query, case) explains a match. For regression models it gives each term’s contribution to the linear predictor and its share of the distance; for random forests, the split variables at which the two cases’ tree paths diverge (#22, #23).
  • predict_survival() predicts survival curves for survival endpoints from the retrieved cases: a Kaplan-Meier estimate over each query’s k nearest training cases, optionally weighted with a tricube kernel (Lowsky et al., 2013). evaluate_survival() scores these predictions on test data with Uno’s C-index and the IPCW (integrated) Brier score, so that k and the distance method can be chosen on held-out data (#21).
  • Out-of-bag and RF-GAP random forest proximities (Rhodes, Cutler & Moon, 2023): proximity_distance(type = c("original", "oob", "rfgap")), distance_random_forest(proximity_type = ) and RFModel$set_distance_method("Proximity", proximity_type = ). RF-GAP removes the in-bag bias of the original proximity, and its proximity-weighted average of the training outcomes reproduces the forest’s (out-of-bag) prediction. RFModel now keeps the in-bag counts by default (#20).
  • Regression models (CoxModel, LinearModel, LogisticModel) support any rms term: splines (rcs(), pol(), …), interactions and so on (#11). Distances are computed in contribution space: each term’s contribution to the linear predictor, c_t(x) = X_t(x) %*% beta_t, compared with a weighted L1 distance. For main effects this is identical to the previous weighted distance (Dippon et al., 2002) (#22).
  • New public field variables holds the data columns used by the formula; terms holds the term labels.
  • get_similar_cases(exclude_self = TRUE) excludes training cases with the same row name as the query, so in-sample queries do not return themselves (#13).

Documentation

  • README and vignettes cover contribution-space distances, survival prediction and evaluation, counterfactual cases, match explanations and OOB/RF-GAP proximities. Corrected the description of the caseId column (the rank of a match) and the proximity and depth formulas (distance sqrt(1 - p); depth is summed over trees; categorical distance is 1 when levels differ).

Internal

  • Removed dead and duplicate C++ code (cpp_weighted_knn(), cpp_orderVector(), unused containers and headers) and fixed compiler warnings (#24, #25).
  • Added value and regression tests for distances and retrieval (#26).
  • Tests use at most 2 threads.
